rationale: SplitEq factored eq for WHIR product sumcheck round 0 (eprint 2025/1117 Sec 3, eprint 2024/1210 Sec 3). Replaced full 2^n eq table materialization with per-point SplitEq reconstruction.
diagnostic: WRONG DIRECTION. SplitEq::get_packed does 1 EFPacking multiply per call. With 2 terms + sparse, inner loop does ~8 EFPacking muls per element (2x w_lo + 2x w_hi). Original code does 1 flat read per element after cheap O(2^n) recursive fill. On M4 NEON the bottleneck is compute throughput not memory bandwidth (IPC=4.33 serial). The factored approach trades cheap memory reads for expensive on-the-fly EFPacking multiplies — net negative. Kill condition should have included: verify compute_eval_eq_packed_dual per-element cost < SplitEq::get_packed per-element cost. DO NOT REATTEMPT SplitEq-based factoring for the product sumcheck weights — the per-element reconstruction cost exceeds flat-table access.

rationale: Delayed-reduction base×ext sumcheck kernel for round 0 (eprint 2025/1117 Sec 4, Plonky3 strategy.rs). Activated dead-code compute_product_sumcheck_polynomial_base_ext_packed replacing sumcheck_quadratic with u128/i128 accumulators.
diagnostic: NO EFFECT. The dead code processes lanes sequentially (for lane in 0..PF::WIDTH) with scalar u64 arithmetic, forfeiting NEON SIMD parallelism. The packed sumcheck_quadratic uses NEON to process all 4 lanes simultaneously. Montgomery reduction savings per lane are cancelled by the 4x throughput loss from scalar-vs-packed operation. On M4 NEON, packed quintic_mul already amortizes Montgomery cost across 4 lanes. DO NOT REATTEMPT scalar delayed-reduction for the product sumcheck — must use NEON-vectorized delayed reduction (e.g. via widening u32×u32→u64 NEON intrinsics) to beat the packed path.

rationale: Fused eq-table generation + round-0 sumcheck dot product (eprint 2025/1117 Sec 5, eprint 2023/1284 Sec 3). Paired lo/hi thread chunks to generate eq weights and immediately compute sumcheck c0/c2 coefficients, eliminating second pass over 1.34 GiB weight table.
diagnostic: WRONG DIRECTION. Halving thread parallelism (16→8 tasks, each doing lo+hi pair) caused ~2x per-task work with only half the thread utilization. On M4 with 10 cores, 8 tasks severely underutilizes the hardware. The dot product add-on per task further increases wall-clock. The original two-pass approach uses full 16-task parallelism for eq generation AND full par_iter parallelism for the dot product — both passes are individually better parallelized. The "saved" second DRAM pass is dominated by the lost thread parallelism. DO NOT REATTEMPT lo/hi thread pairing — cache locality gain is negligible on this scale (40 MiB per chunk >> L2 192 KB) and thread utilization loss is catastrophic. True fusion requires interleaving dot product inside the recursive eq descent itself, not post-hoc pairing.

rationale: Iterative level-by-level eq table doubling replacing recursive binary descent (FOCS 1999, eprint 2025/1117 Sec 3.2). Sequential memory access via ping-pong buffers for two separate eq polynomial arrays.
diagnostic: WRONG DIRECTION. Iterative approach has 12× more memory traffic than recursive. Recursive carries scalars in registers (zero reads, each output written once = 335 MiB). Iterative reads+writes entire growing array at each of 22 levels = ~4 GiB per polynomial. Sequential access does NOT compensate for 12× bandwidth increase. M4 write-combining handles recursive writes well. DO NOT REATTEMPT iterative eq construction — recursive is fundamentally superior due to register-carried scalars.

diagnostic: NO EFFECT. Three compounding problems: (1) corrections table must be full-size (2^24 packed entries = 320 MiB) because sparse statements (memory_acc with inner_num_vars=24) fill nearly the entire weight table — no memory saving; (2) materialize_and_fold_factored after round 0 costs 2^23 × 50 packed muls = 420M (as expensive as original eq generation); (3) factored round-0 inner loop at 64 × 2^17 × 30 packed muls = 250M adds on top. Net compute: ~1.5B packed muls vs original ~500M. The factored approach only wins when corrections are genuinely sparse (few non-OOD statements, small inner_num_vars). DO NOT REATTEMPT factored eq on this codebase — the stacked PCS generates corrections spanning half the weight table.
